transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well… I’m not sure how serious it is, but lately I’ve been having these strange moments where my own house, or sometimes my office, just doesn’t feel quite real. It’s like I’m there, but not fully there—almost like I’m watching myself from across the room. I know that sounds odd… I just thought I should probably ask someone about it.
Have you experienced any other times when you felt detached from yourself or your surroundings, or when things around you seemed unreal?

Yes… I think so. It’s not constant or anything, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there are times at home or at work when the room feels… off, like it’s not quite real. And I’ll have this feeling like I’m sort of watching myself from a distance instead of being fully there. Does that make sense?
Have these experiences ever occurred when you were under a lot of stress or after something traumatic happened, or do they seem to happen out of the blue without a clear trigger?

I’m not totally sure about the trigger, honestly. I mean, I’ve been under stress, but what brings me in is really that I keep having these moments where my house or my office feels unreal—like I’m there, but also kind of watching myself from across the room. It feels strange enough that I thought I should mention it, if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Can you recall if these feelings of unreality or watching yourself started before, during, or after any stressful or traumatic events in your life?

I’m not sure I can pin it to a specific event, to be honest. I don’t want to overstate it. What I can say is that what brings me in is I keep having these moments where my own house or my office feels unreal, like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. I know that may not answer the timing perfectly, but that’s the main thing I’ve noticed.
Have these feelings of unreality or watching yourself ever happened during or after a time of intense stress or a specific upsetting event, or do they seem to happen without any clear reason?

I wish I could give you a cleaner answer. I don’t know that I can tie it to one specific upsetting event. It’s more that these moments keep happening where I’m in my own house or at my office and it suddenly feels unreal, like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. I know that probably isn’t exactly what you’re asking, but that’s the best way I can describe it.
Can you tell me how long these feelings of unreality or watching yourself tend to last when they happen? Do they go away quickly, or do they stick around for a while?

It’s a little hard for me to say exactly. They don’t feel like just a split second, but I don’t think they last, you know, all day either. It’s more like I’ll be at home or in my office and suddenly the place feels unreal, and I have that feeling like I’m sort of watching myself from across the room. Then after a bit I kind of come back to myself. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of timeframe you’re asking for.

Can you tell me if these episodes of feeling detached or watching yourself tend to happen more often during times when you feel particularly stressed, or do they seem to come up even when things are calm and routine?

I think it can happen even when things are pretty normal, honestly. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll just be at my house or in my office, doing ordinary things, and suddenly it feels unreal—like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of really being there. I’m not sure if stress is part of it or not, but I haven’t only noticed it during some big stressful moment.
Can you tell me if these feelings of unreality or watching yourself happen in distinct episodes, or if they feel more like a constant background experience that comes and goes throughout your day?

It feels more like distinct moments, I think. Not like it’s there all day in the background. I’ll be in my house or at my office, just doing something normal, and then suddenly it feels unreal, like I’m sort of watching myself from across the room. Then it passes and I feel more like myself again. I hope that makes sense.

Have you ever experienced any other unusual symptoms during these episodes, like hearing voices that aren’t there, seeing things that others don’t see, or feeling like someone is controlling your thoughts?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, not voices or seeing things, nothing like that. And I don’t have a sense that someone is controlling my thoughts. It’s more just that unreal, detached feeling I was trying to describe. I hope that answers what you mean.

When you feel detached or like you're watching yourself from a distance, do you feel like your body or self is unreal or changed in some way, or is it more that the world around you feels fake or distant?

I think it’s mostly that the place around me feels unreal—like my own house or my office suddenly seems distant or not quite real. And at the same time I feel like I’m sort of watching myself from across the room, if that makes sense. I don’t mean I actually see myself, just… it doesn’t feel like I’m fully there in the moment.
Can you tell me if these episodes of feeling detached or unreality ever happen when you're not under any particular stress or trigger, and if so, how often do they occur?

I think it’s usually tied to feeling stressed, or at least that’s when I notice it most. But… it can happen when I’m just at home or at my office doing ordinary things, not some big obvious trigger. It’s not constant, though. It comes in these moments where the room or place feels unreal and I feel kind of like I’m watching myself instead of being fully there. Then it passes. Does that answer it okay?

Can you tell me if these feelings of unreality or watching yourself have been happening frequently over a longer period of time, like most days for several months, or if they come and go in a way that feels more occasional and less consistent?

It’s more that it comes and goes, I think. I wouldn’t say it’s every day for months or anything like that. It’s just… enough that it’s been bothering me and that’s kind of why I’m here. I’ll be at home or in my office and suddenly the place feels unreal, or I feel like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of just being there. But then it passes. I hope that makes sense.
When you feel like you're watching yourself from a distance, do you feel detached from your thoughts, body, or sense of identity, or is it more that the world around you feels fake or distant?

It’s more the world around me, I think. Like my house or my office will suddenly feel unreal or distant, and then I get this odd feeling like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. I don’t know if that counts as being detached from myself too, but that’s the best way I can describe it.
Can you tell me how often these episodes happen—do they occur several times a day, a few times a week, or more rarely?

It’s not several times a day, no. I’d say it’s more… a few times a week, maybe? Some weeks it feels like less, and I try not to make too much of it, but it does keep happening. I’ll just be at my house or in my office and suddenly things feel unreal, like I’m sort of watching myself from across the room. Then it passes. Is that the kind of frequency you mean?

When you feel like you're watching yourself from a distance, do you also feel detached from your body or as if your thoughts aren't really yours, or does it only feel like the world around you is unreal?

I think it’s mostly that the world around me feels unreal. Like, my house or my office will suddenly seem distant or not quite real, and then I get that strange sense that I’m watching myself from across the room. I don’t know that I’d say my thoughts don’t feel like mine… it’s more like I’m not fully there in the room, if that makes sense.
Have you experienced these feelings of unreality or watching yourself almost every day for at least a month, or have there been periods where they went away completely for a while?

No, not a month. It’s been… about two weeks, I think, since that client threatened me in my office. So it hasn’t been almost every day for a month or anything like that. I guess it’s just felt longer because it’s been unsettling.
Have you felt detached or experienced this sense of unreality almost every day for the past two weeks, or has it been more on and off during that time?

It’s been more on and off, I think. Not every single day, or at least I don’t want to overstate it. But it keeps coming back—those moments where my house or office suddenly feels unreal, and I feel like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of really being there. It’s happened enough that it’s what made me come in, if that makes sense.
Have these feelings of unreality or watching yourself ever lasted for most of the time during a period lasting at least a few weeks?

I don’t think it’s been most of the time, no. It’s more like… it comes in moments. What brings me in is that I keep having these episodes where my house or my office feels unreal, and it’s like I’m watching myself from across the room instead of actually being there. But I wouldn’t want to make it sound like it’s constant for weeks, if that’s what you mean.
